findings: Code vs payload structure (matches): every payload has exactly unit, source_fidelity, corrections, variants, expanded_order_sha256, source_order_sha256, documentary_instructions_sha256 and navigation_sha256, as review_payloads lines 446-448 produce. Each fidelity entry has target, target_end, settings, corrections, attesting_controls, corrected/resolved/literal_sha256 (lines 434-439). Each attesting_controls entry has stem, lang, segment_index, a unit subset of {conditions, marked, instructions, head, opening_page}, a segment subset of OCCURRENCE_CONTROL_KEYS, and enclosing_scopes (lines 83-87). Entries are sorted by (stem, lang, segment_index); for example amidah_qedushah < musaf_qedushah_yimlokh < musaf_repetition_vetimlokh < musaf_repetition_yimlokh.

Owner exclusion vs call-site inclusion (matches the docstring and code): in every pointer payload the reviewed unit lists itself as a caller, with its own segment_index and speaker. That is correct because only `unit is owner` (the canonical host) is skipped. The redirected original source occurrence amidah_qedushah appears as a separate call site, with its unit conditions (recitation repetition=true, quorum minyan=true), its rashi instruction and its own speaker, for qadosh (seg 1), barukh_kevod (seg 3), uvedivrei (seg 4) and ledor_vador (seg 6). In these he payloads it carries the controls that are conditioned in that context.

No repeated recitation is confused with a canonical identity: each segment's callers are keyed on that segment's target. In musaf_repetition_vetimlokh, the prayer target vetimlokh_attah_hashem/vetimlokh has only the self caller. Psalms 146:10 has three callers (musaf_qedushah_yimlokh seg 0 with speaker קו״ח, musaf_repetition_vetimlokh seg 1, musaf_repetition_yimlokh seg 0). The en lists are parallel but have no speakers, which matches the en segments.

Literal/resolved/corrected describe only the owner's own selected printing, as stated: literal==resolved==corrected everywhere except musaf_repetition_uvekhen_ten_pachdekha/en. There the identity-scoped correction rh_pachdekha_hast (identity uvekhen_ten_pachdekha; attestations s27 rh_uvekhen_ten_pachdekha and s251 this unit; before 'all that Thou ', sic 'has', after ' created.') fits the final clause of the own literal and gives corrected != literal == resolved. Unit-local file corrections are picked up through own_file: musaf_veattah_ezon_qol/en 'fortyeight' -> 'forty-eight', and musaf_haochez/he שֶׁחוּא -> שֶׁהוּא before ' רַךְ לִרְצוֹת' (the sic is present in the harachum refrain).

The wording selections agree with the selected printings: qadosh haaretz_with_meteg (הָאָֽרֶץ); barukh_kevod kevod_name_without_maqaf (כְּבוֹד יְיָ); ledor_vador dor_defective (לְדֹר וָדֹר); pachdekha kol_with_maqaf_shiltan (כָּל־ ... שֶׁהַשִּׁלְטָן); kavod land_without_comma (both he and the en 'Thy land happiness' have no comma); Ps 146:10 name_plene_halleluyah_sheva + the_lord_shall_reign (יְהֹוָה ... הַלְלוּיָהּ / 'the Lord shall reign'). uvedivrei, tzaddiqim and qadosh_attah have empty settings. qadosh_attah's canonical_end hamelekh_haqadosh range binds only the self caller.

Effective conditions: every enclosing_scopes list is empty. That is consistent, because none of the recorded callers' segments carry conditions or condition_end_corresp. musaf_haochez/he has a local marked variant condition (hehagui/vehoveh) on a non-canonical segment. It has no source_fidelity, so attesting_controls is not involved.

Non-pointer payloads (vechayyot, veammekha, veattah, tehillot, conclusion_parts, haochez) are included through review_encoding and have source_fidelity=[], which is correct. Their source alternatives, citations, source_notes and speakers are unchanged literal data outside this binding review.

The shared global hashes are the same in all 29 entries: documentary 6f957bfb..., expanded ee5b73a1..., navigation a8da7859..., source_order fc8e3c6b.... As instructed, I defer them to the separate order/encoding review.

Non-blocking observation, not verifiable from the pack: pachdekha, kavod, tzaddiqim, vetimlokh (prayer) and qadosh_attah list only the self caller. The pachdekha correction attestation names rh_uvekhen_ten_pachdekha, and it is absent from the callers. That fits it being the canonical_home owner. prepare_documents lines 458-464 forbid unit or segment controls on canonical_home units, so excluding it drops no controls. I did not read the readings data or _range_segments to confirm that it is the owner.

Non-blocking observation, not verifiable from the pack: amidah_qedushah appears for qedushah segs 1/3/4/6 but not as a Ps 146:10 caller. Under the approved code, this means its yimlokh (if it has one, presumably seg 5) is not pointed at urn:...bible:psalms/146/10 and not covered by any range that includes it. Whether that separate identity is correct is a question about the previously approved data model. The data owner should confirm it if it was not already established.

Minor/cosmetic: Hebrew-only variant settings (for example the meteg and maqaf features) appear in the en fidelity settings, because settings are unit-level (line 419). For en, resolved==literal, so output is unaffected.

Scope limits: I did not have the earlier payloads, so I cannot independently confirm the claim that all 87 old payloads are computationally semantically unchanged. This approval covers only the current content of these 29 payloads against the current code. It does not cover the new batch, the 56 new payloads or exports, or the global order/encoding hashes.
